root_cause.text: The ADIS IIO subsystem’s adis_init() assumed struct adis->ops was always initialized after custom ops support was added, and dereferenced this possibly NULL pointer in zero-initialized struct adis instances allocated by devm_iio_device_alloc().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (!adis->ops->write && !adis->ops->read && !adis->ops->reset)` to `if (!adis->ops)` before accessing member function pointers, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that drivers relying on default ops leave `adis->ops` NULL because `struct adis` is zero-initialized, causing the NULL dereference in `adis_init()`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The ADIS IIO subsystem’s adis_init() assumed struct adis->ops was always initialized after custom ops support was added, and dereferenced this possibly NULL pointer in zero-initialized struct adis instances allocated by devm_iio_device_alloc().
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (!adis->ops->write && !adis->ops->read && !adis->ops->reset)` to `if (!adis->ops)` before accessing member function pointers, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that drivers relying on default ops leave `adis->ops` NULL because `struct adis` is zero-initialized, causing the NULL dereference in `adis_init()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use default ADIS ops only when no ops table is supplied and reject incomplete custom ops tables as invalid.
intent_record.what: The initialization logic was changed from checking whether all three operation callbacks (`write`, `read`, and `reset`) are absent on `adis->ops` to instead checking whether the entire `adis->ops` pointer is NULL before assigning `adis_default_ops`; the existing validation that returns `-EINVAL` when any individual callback is missing remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, default operations are now assigned only when no ops structure is provided at all, while a partially populated custom ops structure is rejected with `-EINVAL` instead of being treated like a missing ops set. This prevents dereferencing `adis->ops` only after confirming it exists and enforces that custom ops must provide all required callbacks.

grouping_result.intent: Use default ADIS ops only when no ops table is supplied and reject incomplete custom ops tables as invalid.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by handling the case where adis->ops may be NULL, assigning default ops only when no table is supplied, and rejecting incomplete custom ops tables to prevent invalid dereferences in adis_init().

candidates.rationale: This line directly dereferences adis->ops without first verifying that the ops pointer itself is non-NULL. In zero-initialized struct adis instances, adis->ops can be NULL, causing the NULL pointer dereference described in the root cause.

This conditional also dereferences adis->ops unconditionally. If adis->ops is NULL, evaluating any of these members will trigger the crash; it is part of the same faulty assumption that ops was always initialized.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences adis->ops without checking whether the ops pointer itself is NULL. In zero-initialized struct adis instances, adis->ops can be NULL, directly causing the NULL pointer dereference described in the root cause.

This statement makes the same unsafe assumption that adis->ops is always initialized and unconditionally dereferences it. If adis->ops is NULL, evaluating this condition will also crash, so it is part of the vulnerable logic.
